Below it, a ruled table: at left a column of Roman regnal numbers, then a column of dates, then the central column of text (prose and entries), then narrow numeric columns at right. Line numbers 10 to 50 stand in the left margin. A small note stands in the right margin near the foot of the table.

main_text.p: tore, inconsideratius velit Armis decernere, ac tam dubium inire belli fortunæ discrimē. Theodericus Imperatoris persuasione ac cōsilio delectatus, ex Thracia Italiam versus iter cum universo Ostro-Gothorum populo suscepit. Quum in Italiam venisset, Odoacrem triplici prælio victum, postremo interfecit. Tum omnibus sibi conciliatis, Gothorum solus & Italicorum Imperium tenuit, Romani tamen Imperatoris nec Insignia, nec Nomen sibi defumsit; sed, quo ad vixit, Rex appellatus est.

main_text.p: Prælio victus à Belisario & Narse, præstantissimis Iustiniani Augusti Ducibus, occisus est; Gothique omnes Italia pulsi circa mensem Maium anno Christi ɔliii. Bello confecto, Gothisque Italia omni exactis, ipsa cum Insulis Sicilia, Sardinia & Corsica Imperio Orientali est attributa; atq; in Victoriæ præmium Narsi ab Imperatore administranda est concessa.
Fl. Narses V. C. Exconf. Magister utriusque Militiæ, pro Imperatore Iustiniano Augusto Imperium Italiæ tenuit annos xvi

page.notes: Marginal line numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 stand at the far left and are not text. The right-margin note "Italia Orientali Imperio concessa:" is set in very small type. Several Roman numerals and dates in the table columns are hard to read in the scan and may contain errors (for example "ɔxxvii", "ɔxxxv", "ɔlii", "ɔliii" stand for Roman dates printed with reversed C or D, read as MDXXVII etc.). Lines containing "//" are ditto marks. The page number "64" is followed by a small superscript mark that I did not reproduce. Some words in the central column, especially in the Latin entries, are blurred and may be misread. Line 12 of the left column ("CCCCXCIV") and similar entries may be misprinted in the original.
